content.text: The text surveys ancient architecture from Persia, Egypt, Assyria, Greece, Etruria, and Rome. It emphasizes Persia’s transition from wooden to stone construction, Persepolis’s columned halls and sculptured staircases, and the influence of Assyria. It argues Egyptians and Assyrians understood arches earlier than traditionally believed. Jewish temples are described as modest shrines enriched chiefly by metalwork. Greek architecture developed from Pelasgic and Asiatic traditions into highly refined Doric, Ionic, and Corinthian orders, exemplified by the Parthenon. Etruscan art is known mainly through tombs and influenced Roman arches and temples. Roman architecture combined Greek orders with Etruscan vaulting, producing monumental basilicas, baths, amphitheatres, tombs, and domes, though often with poor taste. Mary moved to the bathroom. Sandra journeyed to the hallway. John went to the garden. Daniel travelled to the kitchen.
